probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: A monorepo is documented one package at a time and the per-package results are combined afterwards. Package A's public API mentions a class declared in package B. While A is being documented, the compiler sees B only through its compiled declaration files, which carry source maps back to B's TypeScript. After the combine step, A's mention of that class is a working link into B's own documentation, even though every internal numeric identifier was reassigned. Trace how the class's identity is formed when the mention is first converted (including why the location of the compiled output does not matter), how that identity is saved, and how it is matched up again after loading. Then say which code decides whether the mention is drawn as a link on a page.
expectedFacts: Converting a type mention creates an unresolved ReferenceType that carries a ReflectionSymbolId (referenceConverter -> Context.createSymbolReference -> createSymbolId -> createSymbolIdImpl), not a pointer to a reflection, because B is not part of A's project.

CRITICAL: The identity is package name + package-relative path + qualified name. The path part comes from the original source file found by mapping the compiled declaration file through resolveDeclarationMaps (it reads the sibling .map file, takes the first of its sources joined with any source root). The mapping cache is pre-filled by addInferredDeclarationMapPaths, called from getEntryPrograms for the root program and every referenced project, so the identity does not depend on where compiled output lives. The package name is taken from findPackageForPath on the unmapped declaration-file path.

When saving, ReferenceType.toObject writes the numeric reflection id only if the target resolves inside the same project; otherwise it writes symbolId.toObject(), which keeps only package name, package path and qualified name (position and transient id are dropped). ProjectReflection.toObject also writes a symbolIdMap of its own reflections.

Application._convertPackages serializes each package project (serializer.projectToObject) and then calls Deserializer.reviveProjects, which revives each project as a module under one combined project. Each saved symbolIdMap is re-registered in a deferred step (de.defer) after oldIdToNewId is filled - in DeclarationReflection.fromObject for the project-variant branch used when merging, not in ProjectReflection.fromObject - and ReferenceType.fromObject rebuilds a ReflectionSymbolId and points the reference at the combined project.

CRITICAL: ProjectReflection keeps symbolToReflectionIdMap as a StableKeyMap keyed by ReflectionSymbolId.getStableKey(), which omits position and transient id when position is not finite (as for deserialized ids). A's deserialized reference and B's deserialized registration therefore share the key packageName/packagePath/qualifiedName, and the lazy ReferenceType.reflection getter resolves it through getReflectionsFromSymbolId, preferring type-like or value-like kinds according to preferValues.

On the page, formatter.tsx's reference handler uses type.reflection: when it resolves it renders each segment of getUniquePath as an anchor if router.hasUrl(item) (href from urlTo) and as a plain span otherwise; if it does not resolve it falls back to externalUrl or the bare name.

probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: A reader folds the section that lists methods on one class page. On any other class page that same section is folded when they arrive, and in the list of links to the page's own sections in the right-hand column, the matching entry folds in lockstep with the section in the body. Namespace folders in the left sidebar tree, which only exist after the browser builds them from data, are remembered in the same way. Trace how each kind of foldable block gets its identifying name (on the server or in the browser), where the choice is saved and read, how blocks that share a name stay in step, how late-created blocks get the behaviour, and what happens when the browser refuses storage. Finally, spell out the full saved-state name for the methods section in English.
expectedFacts: Body sections: members() and moduleReflection() render every titled section as a details element with class tsd-accordion whose summary carries data-key = 'section-' + section.title; the title comes from getMemberSections (a category title, a group title, or 'group - category'). A section with no title is rendered without a details element, so it has no key.

Sidebar page list: pageNavigation renders each entry of PageEvent.pageSections (filled by startNewSection(title) during the same body render) as a details element with data-key = `section-${title}`, the identical key. The outer page-navigation accordion, the Index accordion and the Settings accordion have no data-key.

Sidebar tree: frontend Navigation.ts buildNavElement creates a details.tsd-accordion with summary.dataset.key = the ancestor names joined by '$'. buildNav then calls window.app.createComponents(container) so the late-created blocks get behaviour; Application.createComponents instantiates each registered component once per element (hasInstance flag), and bootstrap.ts registers Accordion for the '.tsd-accordion' selector.

CRITICAL: Accordion computes its key as 'tsd-accordion-' + (summary data-key, else the lower-cased, dash-joined summary text). A per-key AccordionImpl instance is shared by every accordion with that key on the page; when any of them fires a toggle event all of them are set to the same open state and the value 'true'/'false' is written with storage.setItem. The initial state is the stored value when present, otherwise the element's own open attribute. Because the key is built from the title only, the state is shared by all pages, and the body section and its sidebar entry move together.

storage.ts wraps localStorage in try/catch: if access throws it uses a no-op storage (reads give null, writes are ignored), so default open states apply. window.TypeDoc.disableLocalStorage clears storage and switches to the no-op storage, enableLocalStorage restores the real one, and disableWritingLocalStorage switches to the no-op storage without clearing.

CRITICAL: For the methods section in English the title is 'Methods' (GroupPlugin.getGroups uses ReflectionKind.pluralString(kind) when no group tag is present; kind_plural_method in locales/en.ts), so the saved-state name is 'tsd-accordion-section-Methods'.

probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: In a generated site, a search result, a sidebar entry and a class-hierarchy entry are all created in the browser from data files, yet they link correctly from pages that live at different folder depths. Trace how that works: how each page tells the browser where the site root is and how that value depends on the page's own depth, what form the addresses stored in the data files take and which code writes them, how the browser scripts combine the two, and how the answer changes for the layouts that give every page its own folder. For a class page in the default layout, state the root value its page carries and the exact address the search data holds for one of that class's methods.
expectedFacts: default.tsx sets the html element's data-base attribute to context.relativeURL('./'); DefaultThemeRenderContext.relativeURL calls router.baseRelativeUrl(page model, url), appending a cache-bust query only for asset URLs when requested. The same helper makes the stylesheet and script addresses in the page head.

CRITICAL: BaseRouter.baseRelativeUrl counts the '/' characters in the current page's full URL (getFullUrl) and prefixes that many '../' to the target; for target './' with depth above zero it returns just the repeated '../' (avoiding '.././'), and at depth zero it yields './'.

The directory-style routers (KindDirRouter, StructureDirRouter) override getFullUrl (and relativeUrl) to strip the trailing 'index.html' through fixLink, so a page's URL ends in '/' and depth is counted on that directory form (e.g. 'classes/Foo/' gives '../../').

The addresses stored in the data files are site-root-relative strings taken from router.getFullUrl: JavascriptIndexPlugin.buildSearchIndex (row url), HierarchyPlugin.buildHierarchy (url) and DefaultTheme.buildNavigation (path); members carry an anchor suffix assigned by BaseRouter.buildAnchors/createAnchor from the page's Slugger.

CRITICAL: The browser scripts (Search.ts state.base, Navigation.ts BASE_URL, Hierarchy.ts BASE_URL) read document.documentElement.dataset.base, append a trailing '/' if missing, and build every href as base + stored root-relative url.

For the default 'kind' router a class page is 'classes/<Name>.html', so its page carries data-base '../'. The search row url for a method is 'classes/<Name>.html#<anchor>' where the anchor is the method name passed through the page's Slugger, which lower-cases by default (sluggerConfiguration lowercase: true), so 'getFoo' gives '#getfoo'; the link the script builds from that page is '../classes/<Name>.html#getfoo'.

probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: In a generated site, every little kind icon next to a member name is drawn from one shared graphics file instead of being repeated in each page. Trace how that works end to end: where the artwork for each kind is defined and how a page's markup refers to the shared file, which component writes the shared file and in which phase of the render, why the same artwork also exists as a script, how entries that the browser creates later (sidebar, search results) refer to an icon, and why pages opened straight from disk need special handling. Finally, give the exact fragment reference the sidebar uses for an interface entry, and the letter shown in that icon.
expectedFacts: Artwork: getIcons() in partials/icon.tsx returns one function per ReflectionKind plus named extras (chevronDown, checkbox, menu, search, anchor, folder, alert icons); kind icons are small svg built by textIcon with a letter and a colour variable (interface: letter 'I', var(--color-ts-interface)). DefaultTheme keeps them as theme.icons and getReflectionIcon(reflection) returns the kind unless a custom theme returns another key.

CRITICAL: Each page's DefaultThemeRenderContext builds _refIcons = buildRefIcons(theme.icons, this): every icon except the checkbox is replaced by an svg whose use element points at the shared file ('assets/icons.svg' via relativeURL, then '#icon-<name>'); the checkbox stays inline because CSS targets elements inside it.

IconsPlugin registers its work in postRenderAsyncJobs only when the theme is a DefaultTheme; at the end of the render onRenderEnd writes assets/icons.svg (each icon as a symbol with id 'icon-<name>' and the 'tsd-no-select' class) and assets/icons.js (the ICONS_JS template with the same symbols inlined).

icons.js (loaded with an async script tag in the default layout) waits for the document to be ready, appends a hidden svg holding all the symbols to the body, and, when location.protocol is 'file:', rewrites every use href containing '#icon-' to a fragment-only reference, because external svg references do not work on file URLs.

CRITICAL: Entries created in the browser (Navigation.ts buildNavElement, Search.ts result rows) use fragment-only references '#icon-' + (entry.icon || entry.kind), relying on the sprite that icons.js injected (Navigation.ts and Hierarchy.ts also use '#icon-chevronDown', Navigation.ts '#icon-folder'); the data carries an icon field only when theme.getReflectionIcon differs from the kind (DefaultTheme.buildNavigation, JavascriptIndexPlugin row.icon). Symbol ids use the numeric ReflectionKind, so an interface entry refers to '#icon-256'.

probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: The tool can show its console messages and the generated site in another language. List every place along the pipeline where the chosen language actually takes effect: where it is read and applied for console messages (including when it is set inside a configuration file), how a user's own wording overrides built-in text and what happens for a language with no built-in text, how the names of kinds of declarations, comment tags and flags are translated (and what else those translated names feed into besides display), and what the generated pages and their browser scripts do with the language.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: Application applies the language by calling internationalization.setLocale(lang) after the programmatic options are set, again after the configuration files are read (because the language may come from a config file), and then adds the user's 'locales' entries with internationalization.addTranslations(lang, overrides) once reading is finished; messages logged before the config is read use the earlier locale.

Internationalization.setLocale merges the built-in table for that locale (de, en, fr, ja, ko, zh) with the user's overrides, falling back to the English table for a locale with no built-in text; addTranslations also updates the live table when it is for the loaded locale; Application warns that a language with no translations is unavailable and lists the supported ones (built-in plus any with user entries).

The i18n proxy in utils-common/i18n.ts looks up the message by key and substitutes {n} placeholders (the key itself is returned when it has no entry); translateTagName looks up 'tag_<name>' and otherwise builds an English title-cased name from the tag.

CRITICAL: Kind names go through i18n in ReflectionKind.singularString and pluralString. The plural names become the group titles (GroupPlugin.getGroups) and the default group-order weights (GroupPlugin.setup), so section headings and their order are fixed in the model at conversion time in the language active then; singular names prefix page titles (header.tsx) and feed browser labels.

Tag and flag names: comment.tsx (block tag headings and modifier badges) and navigation.tsx (member-visibility filter labels) call translateTagName, and flag badges and filter labels use ReflectionFlags.flagString (flag_* keys).

Generated pages: the default layout sets the html lang attribute from the language option; AssetsPlugin.getTranslatedStrings builds the window.translations table (interface strings plus kind_<n> singular names) that is prepended to main.js when the render ends, and the frontend scripts (Application.ts, Search.ts, Navigation.ts, Hierarchy.ts) read it, with English defaults in frontend Application.ts for debugging.

probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: After the compiler-driven part of a run, several independent processing steps clean up and enrich the model: removing hidden members, merging modules on request, linking implementers and subclasses, copying inherited comments, grouping, categorising, resolving links, and so on. Give the order in which these steps run at the start and at the end of that stage, how that order is decided (including ties), and which of them run again when a project is restored from previously saved results instead, in what order, with what each repeated step does there. Say also which steps do not run again, and who triggers each of the two situations.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: Order is decided by listener priority: EventDispatcher.on uses insertPrioritySorted, so higher priority runs first and equal priorities keep registration order; registration order is the Converter constructor's plugin construction order (Category, Comment, Group, Implements, InheritDoc, LinkResolver, Package, Source, Type, Include, MergeModuleWith).

Start of the stage (Converter.resolve triggers resolve-begin, then one resolve event per reflection, then resolve-end): MergeModuleWithPlugin (priority 10000) first, then the priority-0 listeners in construction order: CommentPlugin (removes hidden reflections), PackagePlugin (project name/readme), SourcePlugin (source file names and links).

End of the stage: the priority-0 listeners ImplementsPlugin, InheritDocPlugin, TypePlugin (construction order), then GroupPlugin (-100), CategoryPlugin (-200) and LinkResolverPlugin (-300), so implementers and inherited comments exist before sections are built and links are resolved last.

CRITICAL: When a project is restored from saved results, Application triggers the revive event after Deserializer.reviveProjects (in _convertPackages and in _merge). Listeners run in this order: MergeModuleWithPlugin (10000), TypePlugin (100), then ImplementsPlugin, InheritDocPlugin, PackagePlugin (0), GroupPlugin (-100), CategoryPlugin (-200), LinkResolverPlugin (-300). CommentPlugin, SourcePlugin and IncludePlugin do not listen to it because their results were already serialized.

probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: My project has two entry modules which I listed in a deliberate order, one of which also has markdown documents attached, and nothing about ordering is configured. In what order do the modules appear in the sidebar and on the index page, in what order are the members of a class listed within its page, and in what order do the page's sections appear (give the English names of the first three sections on a module page that has documents, classes and functions)? Then explain what changes if the project is told to keep my order, what happens to a class's member order when a comment on that class names an ordering strategy with a misspelled word, and how a section that has no title is treated in the page and in the sidebar.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: The default strategy list is kind, instance-first, alphabetical-ignoring-documents (OptionDefaults.sort). getSortFunction builds a comparator that tries the strategies in turn and the first that distinguishes the two items decides; the kind strategy uses the user's kind order followed by any missing kinds in the default order (Document, Project, Module, Namespace, Enum, EnumMember, Class, Interface, TypeAlias, Constructor, Property, Variable, Function, Accessor, Method, Reference). Documents therefore come first and are never alphabetized, so they keep their original order.

Sections (groups) are not ordered by that comparator: GroupPlugin.sortGroupCallback orders them by weights, which by default are the plural kind names in a fixed order (Documents, Modules, Namespaces, ... - so a module page with documents, classes and functions shows Documents, Classes, Functions in that order); a group-order setting replaces the list and '*' marks where unlisted names go, otherwise unlisted names come last, ties broken alphabetically. When categories exist they are the sections instead (or are nested as 'group - category' when categorize-by-group is on) and are ordered by their own order setting with the same wildcard rule; CategoryPlugin re-sorts each category's children with the same comparator.

CRITICAL: GroupPlugin.group sorts a container's children, documents and combined list only when the keep-entry-order setting is on (default true) or none of its children is a module; so by default modules are sorted alphabetically by name, and when the setting is turned off a container whose children are modules keeps the order in which entry points (or modules) were created and its documents are left unsorted too.

A comment tag naming a strategy on the container replaces the default list for that container only. GroupPlugin.getSortFunction splits the text on commas/whitespace, warns for each invalid name and passes only the valid ones; CategoryPlugin silently drops invalid names. With a single misspelled name the list is empty, the comparator returns 0 for every pair, and the members stay in conversion (declaration) order.

A section titled 'none' (case-insensitive; the single section built when a container has children but no groups, or a group the user named so) is moved first by sortNoneSectionFirst in getMemberSections and rendered without a heading or collapsible wrapper in members.tsx/moduleReflection.tsx; in the sidebar, DefaultTheme.buildNavigation's filterMapWithNoneCollection lists its children first, directly, but only when sidebar grouping or categorising is switched on - by default the sidebar lists the already-sorted children flat.

probes.author: r3x-typedoc-drafter
probes.query: Documentation-coverage warnings are switched on. In my own package a class has a method with no comment at all. My package also re-exports a class that comes from a dependency installed as a third-party package and has no comments. A function elsewhere has a comment consisting of nothing but a visibility-style modifier. For which of these does the tool warn? Explain which kinds of item are checked by default and how functions, accessors and items nested inside a parameter or a type alias are handled, which package list is assumed when I give none and where that default comes from, what counts as 'has a comment', how to silence single items without turning the check off, and what the warning text tells me.
expectedFacts: The check runs only when the 'notDocumented' validation flag is on (default false in the validation option declaration); Application.validate then calls validateDocumentation with requiredToBeDocumented, intentionallyNotDocumented and the package list.

CRITICAL: By default Enum, EnumMember, Variable, Function, Class, Interface, Property, Method, Accessor and TypeAlias are required (not Constructor, Module, Namespace, parameters or type parameters). Functions/methods are checked through their call signatures, accessors through get/set signatures (constructors through constructor signatures if listed); selecting either Function or Method selects call signatures of both; a declaration that has signatures is skipped itself when it is a signature container. A signature counts as documented when its parent has a comment.

Indirections: anything with a Parameter ancestor is ignored; a type literal owned by a type alias, a call signature directly inside a type literal and a construct signature inside an alias are checked by checking the owning alias/declaration instead.

'Has a comment' is Reflection.hasComment -> Comment.hasVisibleComponent called without a not-rendered-tags list: any non-empty summary text, or any block tag at all, counts; a comment made only of modifier tags (such as a visibility modifier) does not, so that function is reported.

CRITICAL: Only reflections with a symbol id whose packageName is in packagesRequiringDocumentation are reported. When the user gave none, Application.validate uses [project.packageName ?? '<unknown>']; project.packageName is set by PackagePlugin.addEntries from the nearest valid package manifest found from the package directory (or the entry points' root). A symbol's package name comes from findPackageForPath in createSymbolIdImpl: the name after the last third-party-folder segment in its path (scoped-aware), otherwise the nearest manifest, so the re-exported dependency class is not reported unless its package is listed.

intentionallyNotDocumented entries are matched against Reflection.getFriendlyFullName() (for a signature, its parent's name); matched items are skipped, and entries that matched nothing produce a validation warning listing them. The reported text is '<name> (<kind>), defined in <package>/<path>, does not have any documentation', logged through validationWarning.
